correctness.rationale: A forced-unit block of (m-a)(n-b) vertices yields weight >= 2k+(m-a)(n-b) when k defenders occupy a rows and b columns; the forced ones do not support defenders. Enumerating all k relative to m proves the sharp 2m bound, with equality only for supported one-per-row / transposed columns for m,n >=4 and explicitly classified additional exceptions on 2x2 and 3x3. Associated-Stirling counting follows by a bijection to labeled row partitions. The included independent graph-based exhaustive finite checker confirms specified small dimensions, without being used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2019 and 2021 quasi-total Roman papers introduce and bound the invariant but do not enumerate optimal rook labelings. The complete 2024 rook domination polynomial counts ordinary dominating sets, not the extra defender-support restriction. Explicit semantic records and complete primary literature comparison identified no implication of the exact nonempty-fiber-size-at-least-two count or exceptional label-1 optima. Related total edge-domination equivalence was searched; its possible unindexed enumeration remains the principal risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact minimum total edge domination enumeration for complete bipartite graphs may be equivalent to the nonexceptional part of the result.

value.rationale: The complete exact count of optimum quasi-total Roman assignments on every rectangular rook graph is a natural first nonzero coefficient of its weight enumerator. A sharp floor-sized defender structure, a polynomial in the larger dimension indexed by associated Stirling partitions, an orientation transition at square boards and 54 exceptional low-order optimum functions provide a motivated structural classification, not a routine substitution or an arbitrary finite slice.
